This is the story of DeWitt Hutchins’s family.
It begins with George Hutchins, in the Dorset village of Broadwindsor in 1532, and comes down 15 generations:
to Salem in Massachusetts, through the Revolution, and north to Vermont and the Canadian line of New York.
Along the way other families married in: the Southworths, down from the Mayflower;
the Watsons, from Lanarkshire by way of Quebec; the Snyders, the Doolittles, the Buchers,
the Muirs and the Hammonds. Among them are five passengers
on the Mayflower, men who stood at Bunker Hill and Saratoga,
and a soldier wounded at Gettysburg. Most of them left little behind: a line in a parish register,
a name in a census, a stone. This film gathers what can still be known of them.
